answer.rationale: Competitive price-cutting creates immediate churn pressure on SMB segment. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is proven effective for SMB acquisition but risks margin erosion and trains price-sensitive cohorts to expect discounting—unsustainable long-term. Referral incentives (memory_57) are proven but slower-acting for immediate retention crisis. Onboarding simplification and activation messaging are proven adoption tools but don't address retention-at-risk cohorts directly. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) offers a strategic pivot: demo-request and sales-assisted flows show superior pipeline quality and conversion. Rather than compete on price in commoditized SMB segment, redirect sales capacity toward higher-ACV enterprise prospects where Northwind has competitive advantage through consultative selling. This shifts revenue mix upmarket, reduces dependency on price-sensitive SMB churn, and builds durable qualified revenue. Run as standard experiment: establish sales-assist workflow for enterprise-qualified inbound, measure pipeline quality and conversion lift, preserve option to supplement with modest SMB pricing response if churn acceleration exceeds acceptable threshold. This preserves long-term margin structure while addressing immediate competitive threat through repositioning rather than race-to-bottom pricing.
